title: Inhibitory circuits control leg movements during Drosophila grooming (Syed, Ravbar, Simpson; eLife RP106446; bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.06.05.597468)
why: Activates 13A and 13B with CsChrimson in adult flies, both intact and headless, using split lines R35G04-DBD with GAD1-AD, R35G04-DBD with Dbx-AD, R11C07-DBD with Dbx-AD, and R11B07-DBD with GAD1-AD. Reports front-leg extension, less grooming, and rhythmic grooming or walking with pulsed light. The source says the lines label subsets: about 6-7 of roughly 67 13A neurons and about 3 of roughly 47 13B neurons per hemisegment. Qualifies only as partial_or_mixed records for a named hemilineage. Coders should judge whether a subset counts.

title: Central processing of leg proprioception in Drosophila (Agrawal et al.)
why: Optogenetically activates 9Aα, 10Bα and 13Bα in adult flies (headless, tethered, and walking on a ball). Reports joint extension or flexion; for 10Bα, no movement in headless flies and slowing in walking flies. The source calls these populations subsets of hemilineages (9Aα-Gal4 lines label mainly 9Aα, maybe some 9Aα2). Named hemilineage subsets, so partial_or_mixed at most.

title: Selective presynaptic inhibition of leg proprioception in behaving Drosophila (Dallmann et al.; Nature 2025; preprint 10.1101/2023.10.20.563322)
why: Activates 9A neurons with CsChrimson in tethered adults walking on a treadmill, using split R30A10-DBD with R12C09-AD. Light is aimed at the left front-leg neuromere and the line labels about 10 neurons, so this is one-sided and a subset. Reports a changed femur-tibia range and slowing. Read only the bioRxiv/PMC version, not the Nature version of record.

title: Extensive and diverse patterns of cell death sculpt neural networks in insects (Pop et al.)
why: TrpA1 activation of MARCM clones of 'undead' postembryonic octopaminergic 0B neurons (TDC2-GAL4 with dronc mutant) in headless adults; 9/17 flies walked. These are clonal, cell-death-blocked neurons rather than the normal hemilineage. The positive control (TDC2>TrpA1) is not named as a hemilineage. Borderline: at most a clonal record.

title: Changes in the cellular makeup of motor patterning circuits drive courtship song evolution in Drosophila (Ye, Walsh, Junker, Ding; Curr Biol)
why: CsChrimson activation of TN1 neurons in intact and decapitated adult males (dsx-GAL4 with 13H01-LexA; TfAP-2-AD with dsx-DBD). Reports unilateral wing extension, vibration and sine song. TN1 is described as a dsx+ subset of 12A origin, not the whole hemilineage. Likely reject unless subsets count.

title: Segmentally repeated ventral nerve cord circuits drive different leg rubbing behaviors in Drosophila grooming (Guo et al.; iScience)
why: REJECT: activates single cell types (LegPNs, called ascending neurons 'from the 5B hemi-lineage AN05B100'; LegPCs, from hemilineage group IN10B014) that cause leg rubbing. These are single identified cell types, not a hemilineage or a named set of hemilineages.

title: Single-cell type analysis of wing premotor circuits in the ventral nerve cord of Drosophila melanogaster (Ehrhardt et al.; eLife RP106548)
why: REJECT: activation is of single wing motoneuron lines only. Hemilineage activation phenotypes (2A, 7B, 11B, 12A, 18B, etc.) are only cited from Harris et al. 2015.

title: Systematic annotation of a complete adult male Drosophila nerve cord connectome reveals principles of functional organisation (Marin et al.; eLife RP97766)
why: REJECT: connectome annotation. Hemilineage activation outcomes are restated from Harris et al. 2015, with no activation of its own. Seen only in search snippets; not opened.

title: Unc-4 acts to promote neuronal identity and development of the take-off circuit in the Drosophila CNS (Lacin et al.)
why: REJECT: uses a 7B split (dbx-DBD with ey-AD) for unc-4 knockout and hid ablation, not activation. 2A/7B activation outcomes are cited from earlier work.

title: Doublesex regulates the connectivity of a neural circuit controlling Drosophila male courtship song (Shirangi, Wong, Truman, Stern; Dev Cell)
why: UNCLEAR, not accessed (paywalled, 403). Uses a 12A-only split (R13H01-AD with R24B02-DBD) for dsx knockdown and TN1A subsets. Snippets did not show whether 12A or TN1 was activated in adults. Needs full-text check.

title: Nested neural circuits generate distinct acoustic signals during Drosophila courtship (Lillvis et al.; Curr Biol 2024, cell.com PII S0960-9822(24)00015-0; journal DOI not verified)
why: Probable REJECT: TN1A activation elicits sine song, but TN1A is a single cell type and the snippets did not name a hemilineage. Not opened.

title: Hemilineage-specific expression of the RHG genes Grim and Reaper sculpt neural network composition during Drosophila neurogenesis (Sproston et al.)
why: REJECT: developmental cell death in 12A; no activation and no adult behaviour.

title: Proprioceptive limit detectors contribute to sensorimotor control of the Drosophila leg (Pratt et al.; Nat Commun)
why: REJECT: activates hair-plate sensory neurons (CxHP8), not a VNC hemilineage.
